parole.significato: A Native American tribe from Delaware.
parole.testo: From Unami ahkinkèshaki (“stony ground”, or “hook mouth”, or “on low ground”), whence also Hackensack.

parole.significato: Apios americana, a perennial vine that bears edible beans and large edible tubers.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Unami hopënis (/hopənis/ (which has now shifted to meaning "potato"), compare Munsee óhpən, ohpën (“potato”)), possibly via Colonial Swedish. Compare katniss.

parole.significato: A light, low, four-wheeled carriage with standing top, open at the sides, but with waterproof curtains for bad weather.
parole.testo: Probably from Rockaway Beach, where they were used. From the Unami lekawe (“sandy place”) or a Munsee cognate of that word.

parole.significato: A shoe, especially a warm, waterproofed boot.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Unami chipakw/chipàkw (“shoe”); the spelling altered under the influence of the English words shoe and pack.

parole.significato: Relating to the geological process which created the Taconic mountain range.
parole.testo: From Tacony (a certain river) + -ic. The river's name is borrowed from Unami tèkhane (literally “cold river”), from tè inan (“cold”) + -hàne (“river”). Other early spellings include Taughkannuc.

parole.significato: A Native American people, one of the three main divisions of the Lenape Nation.
